rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the most important uncertainty is whether multimodal fusion (RNA + image) provides any benefit over single-modality approaches, and what a reasonable baseline accuracy looks like. Config_001 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) is the simplest and most interpretable multimodal configuration: it uses a fast linear RNA representation (PCA), a standard pretrained CNN (ResNet50), and the most basic fusion (concatenation). This establishes a clear baseline that isolates the core question—does combining modalities help at all?—without confounding from complex encoders, multiprofile aggregation, or learned fusion weights. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can systematically upgrade individual components (e.g., scGPT for RNA, ViT for image, weighted fusion). If it underperforms, the result tells us the bottleneck is in representation quality or fusion strategy, guiding more targeted exploration. As experiment 1 of 10, this maximizes information per trial by anchoring the search space with a well-understood reference point.

The only completed experiment (config_001: pca_n2000, resnet50, concat, singleprofile, multimodal) yielded ~52.7% accuracy, a weak baseline. The most impactful single-variable question is whether replacing the linear PCA RNA encoder (pca_n2000) with a learned, context-aware encoder (scgpt) substantially improves representation quality. config_043 changes only the RNA encoder (pca_n2000 → scgpt) while holding image encoder (resnet50), fusion (concat), and profile setting (singleprofile) identical to config_001, giving a clean A/B comparison. This is the best use of experiment 2 because: (1) the RNA encoder is likely the most informative modality for cellular profiling, so its quality is the highest-leverage design choice; (2) a single-variable change from the baseline isolates the effect of the encoder upgrade; and (3) with 8 experiments remaining, establishing whether scgpt is meaningfully better than PCA early will guide whether to invest subsequent experiments in scgpt-based multimodal/multiprofile configurations.

Evidence: config_001 (pca_n2000 + resnet50 + concat, singleprofile) achieved 0.527 acc, while config_043 (scgpt + resnet50 + concat) dropped to 0.427, strongly indicating pca_n2000 is the superior RNA encoder. The only major untested variable in the best config's neighborhood is the image encoder. Question: Does upgrading from resnet50 to the much stronger imagenet_vit_l improve multimodal accuracy? config_047 is an exact single-variable swap from config_001 (only image_encoder changes: resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l; all else identical: multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, None aggregation, concat fusion). This clean A/B test isolates the image encoder effect, which is likely the highest-leverage remaining design choice. If it helps, subsequent experiments can stack it with multiprofile/aggregation or weighted fusion; if it doesn't, we rule out that direction and focus on fusion or profile settings. With 7 experiments left, establishing whether the stronger image encoder pays off is the most information-dense next step.

Evidence: Across 3 experiments, pca_n2000 is clearly the best RNA encoder (0.527 vs 0.427 for scgpt), and imagenet_vit_l is the best image encoder (0.535 vs 0.527 for resnet50). All tested configs used singleprofile with concat fusion. The largest unexplored structural dimension is multiprofile, which could capture richer cellular heterogeneity. Question: Does adding multiprofile with simple avgpool aggregation improve accuracy over the best singleprofile setup (config_047, 0.535)? Why this config: config_049 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + multiprofile + concat) isolates the multiprofile effect by keeping the best-known RNA encoder, image encoder, and fusion method while introducing only the profile change and the simplest aggregation. This controlled test reduces uncertainty about whether multiprofile is a promising direction before investing further experiments in more complex aggregation (transformer) or fusion (weighted) variants. With 6 experiments remaining, establishing whether multiprofile helps is the highest-value next step.

The strongest evidence from 4 experiments is that multiprofile + avgpool aggregation is the dominant factor (config_049: 0.629 vs best singleprofile: 0.535), and pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l is the best encoder combination. The only untested dimension on the current best config (config_049) is the fusion method (concat vs weighted). Config_009 is identical to config_049 except for weighted fusion, making it a minimal, targeted extension that directly tests whether learned fusion weights can improve upon simple concatenation. This is the highest-value next experiment because it exploits the strongest direction with the smallest possible change, reducing uncertainty about the fusion mechanism while preserving all other proven-good settings. With 5 experiments remaining, this low-risk exploitation maximizes the chance of pushing accuracy above 0.629 before exploring larger structural changes (e.g., transformer aggregation or scvi_n200).

The best result so far is config_009 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) at 0.6352 accuracy. The key evidence shows multiprofile >> singleprofile (~0.10 gain), weighted > concat (small gain), and pca_n2000 > scgpt. The remaining untested dimension within this proven architecture is the aggregation method: we've only tested avgpool. Config_037 changes only the aggregation to transformer while keeping all other hyperparameters at their best-known values. This is a single-variable extension of the current best, directly testing whether a more expressive aggregation (transformer) can capture inter-profile dependencies that simple averaging misses. With 4 experiments remaining, this low-risk exploitation step either finds a new best or confirms avgpool is near-optimal, freeing remaining budget for RNA encoder exploration (e.g., scvi_n200).

The current best (config_009, acc=0.6352) uses pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + avgpool + weighted. The evidence strongly supports this architectural backbone: multiprofile >> singleprofile, imagenet_vit_l > resnet50, avgpool > transformer, weighted > concat. The main untested dimension in this optimal setup is the RNA encoder. scgpt performed poorly in singleprofile (0.4275 vs 0.5266 for pca), but scvi_n200 is entirely untested and uses a fundamentally different (variational) representation that may capture complementary biological signal. Config_032 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted) isolates this one variable while preserving all proven-optimal settings. With only 3 experiments remaining, this is the highest-value test: if scvi_n200 matches or beats pca, we identify a new direction; if not, we confirm pca_n2000 is optimal and can focus remaining budget on fine-tuning other aspects.

The current best (config_032, acc=0.706) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted. The key remaining uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation could outperform avgpool specifically with the richer scvi_n200 embeddings. For pca_n2000, avgpool beat transformer by ~5 points (0.635 vs 0.586), but scvi_n200 produces learned, higher-dimensional embeddings where transformer-based attention over profiles may capture non-linear interactions that simple averaging misses. Config_019 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) isolates this single change. If it improves, it opens a new optimization axis; if it doesn't, we confirm avgpool is optimal and can direct the final 2 experiments toward other levers. With only 2 experiments remaining, resolving this high-variance design choice is the best use of budget.

The current best (config_019: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted → 0.725) sits at the apparent optimum across all four design dimensions. The only remaining untested configuration in this top-performing family is config_046 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat). While weighted fusion has outperformed concat in every prior comparison (config_009 vs 049, config_032 vs 018 pattern), the interaction between transformer aggregation and concat fusion has not been directly tested. This experiment clarifies whether concat could produce a complementary effect under transformer aggregation that might marginally exceed 0.725. Given only 1 experiment remains after this one, testing the last unexplored cell in the best family is the highest-value action: it either yields a new best or definitively confirms config_019 as the optimum, allowing the final experiment to be spent on a targeted perturbation if needed.

The current best (config_019, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + multimodal + transformer + weighted. The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l as the optimal encoders, and multiprofile as superior to singleprofile. Within this best-encoder space, we have tested transformer/weighted (0.725), transformer/concat (0.721), and avgpool/weighted (0.706). Config_018 (avgpool/concat) is the only untested aggregation-fusion combination in this top-tier encoder space. While it is unlikely to surpass the current best (since both avgpool and concat are individually suboptimal), it is the most logical exploitation choice: it maintains the two most impactful design decisions (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l) and completes the factorial exploration of the remaining axes. As the final experiment, it provides the cleanest confirmation of the interaction structure between aggregation and fusion within the best-encoder regime, and has the highest expected accuracy among all remaining untested configurations that preserve the proven encoder choices.
